title: Dale Sanders Completes Appalachian Trail at 91
summary:
Dale Sanders has set a hiking record at age 91. On August 31, 2026, the Memphis, Tennessee, resident became the oldest person to complete the entire Appalachian Trail.

The trail stretches 2,198 miles from Georgia to Maine. It crosses forests, mountains and rocky ground. According to the report, hikers must cover the whole route within 365 days to officially finish. They may walk sections in any order and take breaks between them.

Sanders, nicknamed Grey Beard, finished in 359 days. He began on September 6, 2025, at Harpers Ferry, West Virginia, near the trail's middle. He wanted to enjoy Georgia's colorful autumn leaves.

He took a winter break to avoid snow, then returned in spring. He averaged about 12 miles a day, with one rest day each week.

The journey was difficult. After a fall, numbness in his arm led to a hospital visit. Tests showed a pinched nerve, and he was later allowed to continue. His family and supporters encouraged him when he nearly stopped.

Sanders first held this record in 2017, at 82. His friend M.J. Eberhart broke it at 83 in 2021. Sanders then decided to try again.

He credits daily exercise and a positive attitude for his endurance, the ability to keep going through a long effort.
